title: Traffic Pathway Orchestration Slate — prototype for multi-variant routing & rollback
creator: Priya Sharma
description: Build a lightweight interactive prototype (slate) for a Traffic Pathway editor in Redwood Console that supports multi-variant routing (canary + A/B), path-specific safety gates, and a reversible rollback flow with annotated decision context. The goal is to let engineers and PMs compose split rules, preview runtime effects, and rehearse safe rewind scenarios before applying a rollout. This task covers flows, annotated states, accessible interactions for keyboard users, and a short moderated usability test run.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive prototype demonstrates: create/edit/delete split rules across up to 4 variants
Preview canvas shows expected runtime traffic distribution and latency/cost overlays per variant
Rollback rehearsal flow lets user define rewind point, see expected impact, and run a simulated rollback with confirmation annotations
Design handoff assets (Figma) include component specs and motion guidelines; engineering has a clear API contract doc link
Usability test (n=6) completed with summarized findings and at least 3 actionable UI improvements
comments: 2026-02-21 — Priya Sharma: Initial kickoff with PM and Eng; agreed scope is editor + preview + rollback rehearsal. Eng flagged backend needs for preview API (ENG-20421).
2026-02-25 — Emma Liu: First lo-fi flows uploaded to Figma. Highlights: compact rule composer vs. canvas-based drag. Asked PM which approach better fits policy templates.

2026-03-01 — Rafael Ortega (Platform Eng): Reviewed flows — recommended focusing on deterministic preview (no probabilistic simulation) and exposing per-variant metrics from router telemetry. Linked ENG-20421 and ENG-20479.

2026-03-04 — Priya Sharma: Ran quick stakeholder review (Growth, SRE, Platform). Growth asked for experiment assignment labels to persist for attribution. SRE requested an obvious emergency-rollback CTA and a safe-mode toggle.

2026-03-08 — Emma Liu: Mid-fidelity prototype created. Usability test recruit email sent. Noted two unresolved decisions: how to surface chained safety gates, and whether rollback rehearsal should be a modal or an inline timeline.
2026-03-11 — Mike Jensen (Product): Quick feedback — prefer inline timeline for context; ensure keyboard-only users can trigger rehearse/abort. Marked for In Review with ENG for feasibility.

2026-03-12 — Emma Liu: Attached moderated test notes (n=6). Findings: users liked the preview canvas, were confused by implicit default weights, and wanted a 'what-if' slider. Added three follow-up tasks under sub_issues.
decision_log: Use a hybrid UI: compact rule list for quick edits + preview canvas for scenario validation (Decision 2026-02-25)
Preview will be deterministic based on recent router telemetry snapshot rather than stochastic simulation to reduce user confusion (Decision 2026-03-01)
Rollback rehearsal implemented as an inline timeline with 'rewind' scrubber rather than a modal to preserve context (Decision 2026-03-11)
Expose an emergency rollback CTA that bypasses staged safety gates but requires rationale and audit reason (Decision 2026-03-04)
Keyboard accessibility and ARIA masks are required for the prototype so accessibility patterns can be validated during testing (Decision 2026-03-11)
